title: Evolution of Neogene and Quaternary marine Ostracoda, United States Atlantic Coastal Plain: Evolution and speciation in Ostracoda, IV
citation: Cronin, T.M., 1990, Evolution of Neogene and Quaternary marine Ostracoda, United States Atlantic Coastal Plain: Evolution and speciation in Ostracoda, IV: U.S. Geological Survey Professional Paper 1367-C.
notes:
Paleontology paper (ostracode evolution). Pages 79-111: introduction, framework, tables 1-6, discussion and start of systematic paleontology. Unit values are the time-interval ages the author assigns to formations (p. 86) and environmental/faunal remarks for Charleston-area units. Tables 3-5 (species synonyms, ranges, evolutionary statistics) and table 6 (presence-absence by sample; garbled column layout) are not transcribed. Waccamaw Formation is recorded twice (p. 86 interval age and the more specific p. 101 age). No borings, structures, or groundwater data. Systematic paleontology continues in packet 2.
Pages 112-161: rest of systematic paleontology (continues from packet 1), references, plates 1-17. Observations are the South Carolina type localities of the new species (sample sites with quadrangle, lat/long, surface altitude and sample depth); each distinct locality is recorded once. Several new species share a locality (Florence East: L. florencensis, L. carolinensis, B. florencensis; Beaufort: T. mccartanae, P. hazeli, B. hazeli; Wadmalaw Island: B. valentinei). Conflict for a reviewer: p. 114 gives the type locality of Cytherura neusensis (holotype USNM 413963) as Wando Formation, Wadmalaw Island quadrangle, but plate 17 (p. 160) lists that holotype as sample 23, Penholoway; not recorded as an observation. Species distribution lists by formation are summarized only selectively under units. References: only those on South Carolina or Atlantic Coastal Plain stratigraphy/geochronology are recorded; general evolution, Pacific, European and taxonomic references were skipped.
